In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PET-CT is not a reliable method for the detection of mediastinal nodal involvement in patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) and that the sensitivity of this technique for the detection of nodal metastases is significantly lower than the sensitivity for the detection of primary tumor.
PET-CT is not a good screening tool for the detection of lung cancer, but is useful for staging of lung cancer and for the detection of recurrent disease after treatment.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusion of the PET/CT is not as accurate in the detection of hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes.
the fusion PET/CT underestimates the number of hilar nodal involvement in patients who had undergone resection for lung cancer.
the use of fusion PET/CT for staging non-small cell lung carcinoma has been validated in the literature and is now a standard of care for the evaluation of lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PET-CT in the staging of patients with NSCLC should be considered with caution.
the use of positron emission tomography (PET)/CT in the staging of patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) has a significant influence on the management of these patients.

there are some patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) who have a high probability of having a hilar node that is positive for cancer, but who have a negative fusion positron emission/computography (PET/CT) scan.
